## Easing lower-back problems: an adjustable desk {#缓解腰的问题升降桌}

![Adjustable workstation](../../../assets/imported/Yue.Zhou/gongzuotai.jpg)

Before starting my PhD, I already had severe lower-back muscle strain. How should I put it? It is not exactly a major illness, but it torments you all the time. At its worst, I was in so much pain that I could not sleep at night. I went to hospital and was prescribed medication, but the doctor said that managing it myself was necessary and that there was no complete cure. Later I tried running for six months and, surprisingly, the strain got better. It no longer hurts now, though sitting for too long still causes pain. After starting the PhD I no longer felt like exercising, so I bought an adjustable workstation. I recommend one for everyone; it is so useful! You can work standing up and sit down when tired, greatly reducing the harm prolonged sitting does to the lower back.

(Information dated: 30 December 2022)

:::

::: {.contribution authors="jialin-wang"}

## In-depth advice from someone with a severe herniated lumbar disc and cervical problems {#来自重度腰椎间盘突出颈椎病患者的深度建议}

### Adjustable desks can greatly relieve lower-back problems, but cannot solve them completely {#升降桌可极大缓解腰椎问题但不能完全解决}

I have had a herniated lumbar disc for ten years and cervical problems for five. In 2019 my back hurt so much that I could not sit all day, so I put an adjustable desk in the lab and used the computer standing up for three years. This year I put the same desk in my bedroom. But standing for long periods is as bad for the back as sitting, and eventually standing hurts just as much. An adjustable desk is not a long-term solution: standing merely changes the angle at which you continue to wear out your lower back.

You cannot rely entirely on the desk. I depended on it too much over the past few years, and now prolonged standing hurts as much as sitting. When I had an MRI, the doctor even asked whether I had fractured a vertebra. To genuinely relieve back pain, avoid both prolonged sitting and prolonged standing. One reason secondary-school teachers are prone to back pain is the long hours they spend standing to teach.

In summary, an adjustable desk is useful, but should not be used as a permanent replacement for sitting at a computer. Alternate between the two, and exercise more regularly.

A practical point: adjust the height occasionally. I did not adjust the desk in my lab for several years, and apparently the hydraulic strut rusted. It would no longer move, effectively turning it into an ordinary desk.

### External monitors: preventing and relieving neck problems {#外接屏避免和缓解颈椎病}

One unpleasant aspect of cervical problems is that looking down for too long makes your neck hurt. Even when out on the metro or high-speed train, I have to hold my phone upright at eye level, or I cannot use it for long.

Another method I can suggest for prevention and relief is not to use a laptop for prolonged periods. Looking down at the screen for too long can lead to cervical problems. The same applies to looking down at a phone.

If you frequently use a laptop, put an external desktop monitor in both your bedroom and your office.

My own neck problems started after a year of intensive laptop use. Once I switched to external monitors, they stopped getting worse.

If you use a laptop intensively without an external monitor, it is just as much a neck killer as looking down at your phone all day. Whenever I see people using laptops for long stretches in the lab, I urge them to use an external monitor.

A laptop stand is another option, and cheaper than a monitor. But if your eyesight is poor, an external monitor is still preferable because laptop screens are small and tiring for the eyes. I used to buy lots of laptop stands; now I use them to hold monitors, with the laptop fitting conveniently underneath.

*In my bedroom I use an adjustable desk with a laptop stand. This combination suits someone like me who mainly uses a laptop.*

![Standing desk and laptop stand](../../../assets/imported/Jialin.Wang/shengjiangzhuo.jpeg)

### The best solution: change your habits and exercise more {#最好的解决方案改变生活习惯加强锻炼}

I suggest that people with herniated lumbar discs and cervical problems exercise more. But do not blindly head to the gym. Swimming is the best form of exercise, because most other activities require exerting the lower back and can worsen the pain.

At present, my back only occasionally hurts so much that I cannot bend over. I also know someone whose back pain made him limp when walking. He improved gradually through exercise too.

If you struggle with self-discipline, joining the university swimming club is an option. At least having people to exercise with regularly can provide motivation.

For memberships, I remember that Dushu Lake Swimming Pool offers half-price annual passes each September. But the university club is very inexpensive and better value. Before buying a swimming pass, I used to go once or twice a week with the club. After buying an annual pass, I went fewer than five times in a year, and even less after that. If you have the self-discipline, daily exercise is the best approach. If you cannot keep it up or change your habits, the problem will keep getting worse.

Finally, if your back pain is fairly severe, consider visiting a hospital's orthopaedics department when you have time and having an MRI to find out how far the condition has progressed and determine a suitable recovery approach. Back pain is now very common among young people.

(Information dated: 30 December 2022)
